report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Render drift report; snapshot digest, bytes, load/write; remedy text per drift kind.

symbols.name: counts
symbols.note: Returns sorted dict of counts per item kind.

symbols.name: render
symbols.note: Renders human-readable drift report; first-run and normal branches.

symbols.name: _SNAPSHOT_NOTE
symbols.note: Constant note embedded in snapshot; says only acceptances may be hand-edited.

symbols.name: DIGEST_KEY
symbols.note: String key 'digest' used in snapshot dict.

symbols.name: _MECHANICAL_KEYS
symbols.note: Tuple of keys covered by digest; excludes acceptances and note.

symbols.name: _digest
symbols.note: Computes sha256 digest over mechanical keys with canonical JSON.

symbols.name: digest_ok
symbols.note: Checks whether doc's digest matches computed digest; handles non-dict and __error__.

symbols.name: snapshot_bytes
symbols.note: Serializes snapshot dict with sorted fields, digest, trailing newline.

symbols.name: load_snapshot
symbols.note: Reads JSON file; returns dict or None; returns {'__error__': str} on OSError/ValueError.

symbols.name: write_snapshot
symbols.note: Writes baseline snapshot excluding accepted items; creates parent dirs.

symbols.name: _remedy
symbols.note: Returns remediation text for each drift kind.

claims.text: A hash over the mechanical half only. ``acceptances`` is excluded because it is the one part a human is SUPPOSED to write; ``note`` because it is a constant.
claims.why: _MECHANICAL_KEYS does not include 'acceptances' or 'note'; body built only from those keys.

claims.text: Canonical JSON with sorted keys, so the digest is a function of the values and not of the writer's key order -- two runs over an unchanged tree still produce identical bytes.
claims.why: json.dumps uses sort_keys=True and fixed separators; body keys are fixed by _MECHANICAL_KEYS.

claims.text: ``repo_state`` is INSIDE, and that is not an accident.
claims.why: 'repo_state' is in _MECHANICAL_KEYS and included in body.

claims.text: the digest changes on every commit even when no list moved -- which is correct: the snapshot really does describe a different tree.
claims.why: Whether repo_state changes on every commit depends on the caller's state; not observable in this chunk.

claims.text: Any verb that INHERITS lists from an existing snapshot rather than rescanning has to ask this first and refuse on a mismatch -- otherwise it re-signs whatever a text editor left behind and turns a caught hand-edit into a valid baseline. ``daedalus map --accept`` is exactly such a verb.
claims.why: The docstring names callers outside this chunk; digest_ok itself only returns a boolean.

claims.text: The exact text of the snapshot. Sorted, no timestamps, trailing newline: two runs over an unchanged tree must produce byte-identical output or the git diff -- the thing a human actually reads -- becomes noise.
claims.why: All list fields are sorted; no timestamp key is added; json.dumps output ends with '\n'.

claims.text: ``repo_state`` comes out of ``state``, not out of a probe taken here, so this stays a pure function of its arguments.
claims.why: Only state.get('repo_state') is used; no I/O or clock in this function.

claims.text: A clock reading would not: ``generated_at`` is absent from this artifact on purpose
claims.why: No 'generated_at' key is added to doc.

claims.text: Write the baseline, EXCLUDING every item that has an acceptance entry.
claims.why: keep() filters each list against accepted_keys; accepted items are removed from the kept dict.

claims.text: If an accepted island were baked into ``islands``, ``--refresh`` would silently become a third, undated way to accept -- and being the easiest one, it would be the only one anybody used.
claims.why: Whether --refresh is a way to accept depends on callers of write_snapshot outside this chunk.

claims.text: Keeping accepted items out of the baseline means they stay live drift, suppressed only for as long as their date holds.
claims.why: The 'date holds' behavior depends on check() and acceptance expiry logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: the one that grew to 55 the last time nobody watched it
claims.why: Historical/anecdotal claim; no supporting data in this chunk.

claims.text: 'since' may not be in the future and 'until' may be at most MAX_HORIZON_DAYS days after 'since'; the item comes back when it passes.
claims.why: The enforcement of these rules is in acceptance parsing/validation not shown here; render only prints the text.

observations.what: render() reads self.state.get('counts') rather than using self.counts property; if state lacks 'counts', head is empty even though self.counts would compute it.
In render(), the first-run branch prints 'unknown (nothing reaches them...)' label but uses key 'unknown'; the label text says 'unknown' and the key is 'unknown' -- consistent.
In render(), the 'shims nothing reaches' label uses key 'shims' but the label says 'shims nothing reaches'; the data may include shims that are reached, but the label is just descriptive.
write_snapshot's keep() prefix concatenation assumes item strings start with the prefix; if a state value is not prefixed, it is always kept.
write_snapshot recomputes counts after filtering; but the 'modules' count is taken from kept.get('modules') which is not filtered by acceptances, so accepted modules are still counted.

In snapshot_bytes, 'repo_state' is sorted with dict(sorted(...)) which sorts by key; if repo_state contains non-string keys, sorting may raise TypeError, but repo_state is expected to be a dict of strings.
_digest uses ensure_ascii=False; if any value contains non-ASCII characters, the byte representation is UTF-8; this is deterministic but might differ from a reader's expectation of ASCII.
digest_ok returns False for non-dict or __error__; it does not distinguish 'no digest' from 'mismatch' -- both return False.

write_snapshot writes with newline='\n' but uses p.write_text(text) where text already ends with '\n'; the newline parameter may not affect the text written, but the output ends with exactly one newline as documented.
_remedy has no default/else branch; if a new kind is added without a corresponding remedy, it returns None, which would be rendered as 'None' in output.

risks: render | low | head uses state.get('counts') not self.counts; if state lacks counts, report shows empty head even though counts property would compute it | check whether render is ever called with state missing 'counts'
write_snapshot | medium | modules count is not filtered by acceptances; accepted modules still count as modules in baseline | inspect whether modules can be accepted; if not, this is harmless
_remedy | medium | no default branch; unknown kind yields None and render prints 'None' | check whether all possible kinds are covered; if new kinds are added, this breaks
digest_ok | low | returns False both for missing digest and mismatch; callers cannot distinguish | check whether callers need to distinguish
snapshot_bytes | low | sorting repo_state may raise if keys are not comparable | verify repo_state is always a dict with string keys
